catalog_quote: Stress is nonphonemic, occurring within the stress group on the penultimate syllable or, in certain defined sequences, either on the final syllable, both final and penultimate syllables or on both final and antepenultimate syllables. ... The sequence in which the predominant pattern is penultimate stress is the stress group, or word. ... 1.2 Stress within the word. The predominant pattern within the word is for penultimate stress. ... 1.21 Word final stress. Words which have final stress are divided into two categories: those which always have final stress and those which have final stress if in utterance medial position. Utterance finally there is free fluctuation between final and penultimate stress, penultimate stress occurring more frequently when the onset of the primary intonation contour is emphasized. 1.211 Words with final stress only. When the vowel of the penultimate syllable is followed by a semi-vowel at the same point of articulation stress is always final ... 1.212 Final stress in utterance medial position. The following sequences have final stress if in utterance medial position. Utterance finally or in isolation there is fluctuation between final and penultimate stress. They are listed according to the vowels of each syllable and the consonant which begins the final syllable.

new_statements.quote: Stress is nonphonemic, occurring within the stress group on the penultimate syllable or, in certain defined sequences, either on the final syllable, both final and penultimate syllables or on both final and antepenultimate syllables. One or more of certain stressed syllables may occur following the stress group. Grammatically these syllables are post-clitics. They are not part of the stress group which precedes them. The sequence in which the predominant pattern is penultimate stress is the stress group, or word. [...] 1.2 Stress within the word. The predominant pattern within the word is for penultimate stress.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive and by default penultimate within the stress group (word base plus affixes); post-clitics (da, pa', ma, pronouns ka, ku, nu, din, dan, etc.) bear their own stress outside the group. Lexically/segmentally defined exceptions: (a) penult vowel followed by a homorganic semivowel -> always final stress ([mari'u?] 'far', [lu'al] 'outside'); (b) a long list of specific V-C-VC shapes take final stress utterance-medially but fluctuate final~penultimate utterance-finally; (c) stressed suffixes -an, -i, -ay, -a produce double stress (final+penultimate after the (b) shapes, otherwise final+antepenultimate); reduplicated bases copy the base pattern. Intonation-contour onset is on the penult of the phrase and can override stress utterance-finally.
new_statements.secondary_stress: No secondary word stress as such; describes double-stressed words (final+penultimate, final+antepenultimate) with stressed suffixes, and a possible secondary intonation contour two syllables before the primary one in phrases of 5+ syllables (fn.6: not determined whether predictable).
new_statements.exceptions: Sec. 1.211 words with final stress only (penult V + homorganic semivowel); 1.212 ~40 segmental templates (e.g. -ahaC, -asaC with final semivowel, -itiC, -ikit, -inaC, -uhat..) with final stress utterance-medially, free fluctuation utterance-finally; 1.22-1.23 stressed suffixes -an/-An/-i/-ay/-a giving final+penultimate or final+antepenultimate stress; post-clitics always stressed but outside the stress group.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the 'stress group' = word base + affixes, excluding post-clitics; utterance-final position shows fluctuation because the primary intonation contour (onset on phrase penult) can disrupt the stress pattern. Data from Kibudtungan, (North) Cotabato, fieldwork late 1950s.
new_statements.identity_note: Shand's typescript describes the Ilianen Manobo of Kibudtungan, (North) Cotabato — the same locality as Reid 1971's list and the Brichoux/Shand/Wrigglesworth SIL corpus; this is ilia1236 proper (no dialect split in Glottolog). Author identity: Jean Shand = Barbara Jean Dawson (later publications under Dawson); Felicia Sadowski = Felicia Brichoux.
